title: Rijeka with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Ferries, Entry
metaDescription: Rijeka with a dog in 2027: two official dog beaches, leash rules, Jadrolinija ferry pet rules, accommodation fees, best months, vet basics and EU entry rules.
content:
## Dog beaches in Rijeka

Rijeka has two official dog beaches, both set up by the city.

### Kantrida (Plaža za pse Igralište)
The first dog beach covers about 500 m² on the embankment east of the auxiliary Kantrida football stadium, next to the car park. Parking is free. Facilities include a sunbathing area, a sea entrance, a bench, a waste bin with bag dispenser, running water and a shower with a rubber hose for washing dogs. Swimmers without dogs may use it too, so expect mixed company.

### Brajdica
The second beach is a gravel beach at Brajdica, near the entrance of the D-404 road tunnel, below the tennis courts at Pećine. It is reached by road or by stairs from the street Šetalište XIII. divizije. A fence keeps dogs off the road above. It has a bench, bins, a tap, a shower and a dog-wash hose. There is no shade and no beach bar, so bring an umbrella and water. Cargo ships work in the background. Visitors describe the water as clear and the sea entrance as free of sharp rocks, which makes it the easier of the two for older dogs.

### Other dog beaches nearby
Kostrena, just south of Rijeka, has Mikulova kava, a beach for both swimmers and dogs. Crikvenica, about 35 km southeast, has Monty's Dog Beach and Bar, a themed beach with a bar and organised dog events. Part of Vela plaža in Baška on Krk is also pet-friendly.

## Are dogs allowed on other beaches in Rijeka?
As a rule, no. Outside designated dog beaches, dogs are not welcome on managed city beaches, and local rules require a leash on every public area. Even on the dog beaches the owner must keep the dog on a leash, carry cleaning supplies, pick up waste and rinse the spot where the dog urinated. Quiet rocky coves along the Lungomare and the Kostrena coast are tolerated in practice in the off-season, but signage on site decides.

## Dogs in the old town, restaurants and parks
Rijeka has no formal old town; the Korzo and the surrounding streets are the historic centre. Dogs are allowed on the Korzo and in public squares if leashed. Dogs designated as dangerous must also wear a muzzle.

For off-leash time, the city has seven fenced dog parks. Most have a double gate with a vestibule where the leash comes off. Škurinjska draga (Ulica Petra Kobeka) was the first; Podmurvice (Ulica Plase, 600 m²) has agility equipment. New parks are being built at Grbci, Dražička ulica and Kozala.

Restaurants and cafés in Croatia decide for themselves. Terraces usually accept a leashed dog; indoor dining rooms and food shops often do not. Ask before sitting down, and choose an outdoor table.

## National parks and nature parks
Rijeka itself is a city, but the nearest large protected areas are Risnjak National Park and Učka Nature Park. Leashed dogs are generally allowed in nature parks such as Učka. Many national parks restrict or prohibit dogs, or require a leash and a fee, so check the park's current rules before going. Plitvice and Krka are more restrictive than Učka.

## Ferries and catamarans
The main operator, Jadrolinija, has its headquarters in Rijeka. Transport of pets on its ferries and ships is free. The rules are strict:

- Dogs must wear a muzzle (except assistance dogs) and be on a leash.
- Pets up to 8 kg may enter indoor passenger areas in a carrier of 45 × 35 × 25 cm with a waterproof bottom.
- Larger dogs stay on the open deck on car ferries.
- On catamarans, larger pets travel in a box on the open deck. A fee applies under the official price list and a reservation is mandatory.
- On the larger international ships, dogs can stay in cabins and kennel space is limited. Book early.

A muzzle is the item most visitors forget. Pack one even if the dog never wears it at home.

## What accommodation charges for a dog
Most pet-friendly apartments and hotels in the Kvarner area charge a cleaning or pet fee. Typical amounts are €10–€20 per night in hotels and €30–€60 per stay in private apartments, and some hosts accept dogs for free. Campsites usually charge a daily fee for the dog. Always confirm the fee, size limits and number of dogs in writing, and ask whether dogs may be left alone in the unit.

## Summer heat and best months
July and August bring hot days, often above 30 °C, and asphalt gets hot enough to burn paws. Walk before 9:00 or after 19:00 and avoid leaving a dog in a parked car. The best months with a dog are May, June, September and October, when the sea is warm enough for swimming and the temperatures are comfortable for long walks. Winter is mild enough for walking, and the Lungomare coast path is quiet.

## Vet basics
A microchip is mandatory for all dogs in Croatia. Rabies is the only vaccination required for EU entry. Veterinary clinics operate in Rijeka, and an emergency visit typically costs more outside normal hours. Bring the pet passport, ask your own vet for a note about chronic medication, and take tick and flea protection. Ticks are common in wooded areas such as Učka, and sandflies are present on the coast in summer. Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment for dogs entering.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in
A dog travelling from another EU country needs three things:

1. An ISO 11784/11785 microchip, implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination.
2. A rabies vaccination, with a wait of at least 21 days after the primary shot before entry. The minimum age for the first shot is 12 weeks.
3. An EU pet passport from an authorised vet. In Croatia it costs €10.06 + VAT.

Croatia is in the Schengen area, so there are no routine border checks on the road from Slovenia, but the dog's documents may still be checked. Travellers from Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina or Montenegro face extra checks, and a rabies titre test is required from Serbia and Montenegro. The UK uses an Animal Health Certificate instead of a passport.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Rijeka?
Rijeka rates 3.5 out of 5. It has two official dog beaches, seven fenced dog parks, a free pet policy on ferries and easy road access. It lacks the beach bars, dog menus and wide beach access found in resorts like Crikvenica. Brajdica is the better beach for swimming and Kantrida the more convenient one. Rijeka suits a dog owner who wants a city base with day trips to Krk, Učka and the coast. It is not a destination for those who want unrestricted beach time with a dog.

faq.question: Does Rijeka have a dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes, two: Kantrida (also listed as Igralište) next to the Kantrida auxiliary stadium, and Brajdica near the D-404 tunnel entrance. Both are free, have a shower and a dog-wash hose, and require a leash.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on ferries in Croatia?
faq.answer: Yes. Jadrolinija carries pets free on ferries, with a muzzle and leash required. Dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck, and on catamarans they travel in a box for a fee and with a reservation.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia from the EU?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a rabies vaccination given at least 21 days before travel, and an EU pet passport. The microchip must be implanted before or on the day of the rabies vaccination.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Rijeka with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June, September and October. The weather is mild, the sea is warm and the paths are not too hot. July and August are hot, and walks work best early in the morning or late in the evening.

faq.question: Do dogs need to be on a leash in Rijeka?
faq.answer: Yes, on all public areas, including dog beaches, except inside the fenced dog parks. Owners must carry waste bags, and dogs classed as dangerous must wear a muzzle.

faq.question: Can dogs go to restaurants in Rijeka?
faq.answer: Usually only on outdoor terraces, and at the venue's discretion. There is no general rule, so ask before sitting down.

quickAnswer: Rijeka is moderately dog-friendly. The city has two official dog beaches (Kantrida and Brajdica), seven fenced dog parks and free pet transport on Jadrolinija ferries. Dogs must be leashed in all public areas outside those parks. Entry from the EU needs a microchip, rabies vaccination at least 21 days earlier, and an EU pet passport.
